phase-plan.purpose: Define the shared authored world contract using the user's actual concepts. The contract must let DungeonBreak and Escape the Dungeon share the same evolving game model, with `level` as the shared loadable concept, `room` as a real authored concept, and regions/floors/towns/wilderness/outskirts/dungeons represented without pretending they are all the same thing.
phase-plan.scope: In scope: authored world concepts, document boundaries, generated output shape, stable identifiers, level-to-level transitions, and compatibility with Unreal level workflows. Out of scope: converting all current layouts, final authored region content, or implementing a finished spatial editor.
phase-plan.definition-of-done: Done when the shared `level`-centered contract, room relationship, generated output contract, and transition rules are explicitly defined and recorded for later implementation.

file.description: Existing generic schema baseline that future spatial docs and generated classes will extend rather than replace.
Current gameplay layout source that will later be translated into the level-centered shared contract instead of remaining a one-off format forever.
Plugin baseline that needs a neutral placement payload and diagnostics contract rather than game-specific ad hoc data.

task.description: Define the shared authored concepts that both games can share without semantic drift.
Define the generated output contract used by Unreal and runtime consumers.
Define the split between shared level/room world docs and game-specific semantics.

questions.question: The exact translation order from current Escape the Dungeon layouts and future DungeonBreak region layouts into the shared contract is deferred to later execution work.

decision.summary: `Level` is the shared loadable world concept. A level can represent a dungeon floor, a region, or another authored world state.
decision.impact: Codegen and runtime loading can use one shared concept while keeping level kind semantics explicit.

decision.summary: `Room` is a real authored concept and remains part of levels, especially for dungeon content.
decision.impact: Schema and generated outputs must preserve room-aware authoring instead of flattening rooms into generic placement mechanics.

decision.summary: Levels may have kinds such as `region`, `floor`, or other authored world forms. A region-level contains town, wilderness, outskirts, and dungeon structure, while dungeon progression can still move into later levels that are floor-like or region-like.
decision.impact: Dungeon progression can move from floor-based play to region-like play without changing the loading model, and regional play keeps its own internal authored structure.

decision.summary: Generated outputs should be organized around levels, rooms, transitions, entities, and related content for those levels rather than around invented neutral container nouns.
decision.impact: Generated classes and data will be easier to understand and map to gameplay and Unreal authoring.

suggestion.gap: REQUIREMENTS.xml does not yet explicitly name `level` as the shared loadable concept or `room` as a real authored concept inside levels.
suggestion.proposal: Add a requirement that the shared world model is level-centered, that rooms remain first-class authored data, and that levels can represent floors, regions, and other world forms.
